mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT through t-0w indicates fewer weekday trips and looser commuting constraints; as those declines continue, retail and recreation mobility should keep rising over the next four weeks because more discretionary stopovers occur during recovered trip chains.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below their t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns positive and stays elevated, routine household trips spill into nearby retail errands and improve street activity, which lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks; if grocery trips retreat first, the retail uplift fades.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 and remains above 0 for 2 consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM stays positive for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases daytime circulation and store-access opportunities, so retail and recreation mobility rises over the next month; the effect is stronger when both series improve together than when only one does.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trend upward from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent PARKS recovery signals warmer-weather leisure substitution that diverts some discretionary outings toward outdoor spaces, lowering retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks if PARKS continues to rise while retail stays suppressed.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from its t-1w mean and stays above that level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining elevated relative to t-1w.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps falling while WORKPLACES remains depressed, more people are spending less time at home and more time in mixed-purpose trips, which should push RETAIL_REC higher within one week through opportunistic shopping and errands.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below its previous weekly mean while WORKPLACES stays at least 10 points below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next 7 days after RESIDENTIAL drops and WORKPLACES stays weak.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid improvement in TRANSIT from deeply negative levels marks easing mobility friction; once TRANSIT recovers by more than 15 points from its recent low, retail and recreation mobility should rise over the following two weeks because more cross-district shopping trips become feasible.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 15 points from the prior 2-week trough
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after a >15-point TRANSIT recovery from its recent trough.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both rise together, routine and leisure foot traffic saturate non-retail destinations and pull discretionary visits away from malls and shopping streets, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remain elevated or continue rising.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a continuing RESIDENTIAL decline and a continuing WORKPLACES recovery indicates a shift back to out-of-home routines; if that pattern persists for four weeks, retail and recreation mobility should keep moving up because daily errand chains are rebuilt around commuting.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for 2 consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES rises for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL falling and WORKPLACES rising for two consecutive weeks.
